original_question: Let A_q^{diag} denote the current algebra obtained from the quotient of the reflection equation algebra discussed in the paper, with current modes K_k, K_{k+1}, Z_{k+1}, and Z̃_{k+1}. Let the augmented q-Onsager algebra be the algebra generated by K_0, K_1, Z_1, and Z̃_1 subject to the displayed commutation and higher q-commutator relations in the paper. There is also an explicit homomorphism from the augmented q-Onsager algebra to a coideal subalgebra of U_q(\hat{sl}_2) sending K_0 to ε_+q^{h_1}, K_1 to ε_-q^{h_0}, Z_1 to (q^2-q^{-2})(ε_+q^{-1}e_0q^{h_1}+ε_-f_1q^{h_1+h_0}), and Z̃_1 to (q^2-q^{-2})(ε_-q^{-1}e_1q^{h_0}+ε_+f_0q^{h_1+h_0}). Show that the infinite-dimensional algebra A_q^{diag}, the augmented q-Onsager algebra, and that coideal subalgebra of U_q(\hat{sl}_2) are isomorphic.

refined_question:
Let \Bbb F be a field containing q, \epsilon_+, \epsilon_- and assume that q is not a root of unity. Write [X,Y]_q = qXY - q^{-1}YX. Let \mathcal O_q^{\mathrm{aug}} be the augmented q-Onsager algebra generated by K_0, K_1, Z_1, \widetilde Z_1 subject to
[K_0,K_1]=0,
K_0Z_1=q^{-2}Z_1K_0,\quad K_0\widetilde Z_1=q^2\widetilde Z_1K_0,\quad K_1Z_1=q^2Z_1K_1,\quad K_1\widetilde Z_1=q^{-2}\widetilde Z_1K_1,
and
[Z_1,[Z_1,[Z_1,\widetilde Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=\frac{(q^3-q^{-3})(q^2-q^{-2})^3}{q-q^{-1}}\,Z_1(K_1^2-K_0^2)Z_1,
[\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=\frac{(q^3-q^{-3})(q^2-q^{-2})^3}{q-q^{-1}}\,\widetilde Z_1(K_0^2-K_1^2)\widetilde Z_1.
Let A_q^{\mathrm{diag}} denote the current algebra obtained from the quotient of the reflection equation algebra described immediately before Problem 1-b, generated by its current modes K_\bullet, Z_{\bullet}, \widetilde Z_{\bullet} in the paper's notation. Let B_{\epsilon_+,\epsilon_-}^{\mathrm{diag}}\subset U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2) be the coideal subalgebra generated by the image of the homomorphism
K_0\mapsto \epsilon_+ q^{h_1},\qquad K_1\mapsto \epsilon_- q^{h_0},
Z_1\mapsto (q^2-q^{-2})(\epsilon_+ q^{-1}e_0 q^{h_1}+\epsilon_- f_1 q^{h_1+h_0}),
\widetilde Z_1\mapsto (q^2-q^{-2})(\epsilon_- q^{-1}e_1 q^{h_0}+\epsilon_+ f_0 q^{h_1+h_0}),
with the same coproduct convention as in the paper. Prove that A_q^{\mathrm{diag}}, \mathcal O_q^{\mathrm{aug}}, and B_{\epsilon_+,\epsilon_-}^{\mathrm{diag}} are pairwise isomorphic as associative algebras, and determine explicit polynomial formulas expressing the current generators of A_q^{\mathrm{diag}} in terms of K_0, K_1, Z_1, \widetilde Z_1 (equivalently, the polynomial relations implementing the identification of A_q^{\mathrm{diag}} with \mathcal O_q^{\mathrm{aug}}).
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's Problem 1-b, not at a neighboring statement: the paragraph immediately before Problem 1-b introduces the augmented q-Onsager algebra by its generators and relations, then introduces A_q^{diag} as the current algebra coming from a quotient of the reflection equation algebra, and then displays the homomorphism into a coideal subalgebra of U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2). Problem 1-b then asks exactly for the isomorphism among these three algebras, plus the polynomial formulas relating A_q^{diag} and the augmented q-Onsager algebra. Your draft is close, but it omits that second clause and leaves implicit the assumptions q not a root of unity, the q-commutator convention, the dependence on \epsilon_\pm, and the fact that the paper states this as an open problem. The paper has no Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; Problem 1-b is therefore the nearest official formulation.
